# BK7258 Worktree Build

## Complete workflow

Prefer the bundled end-to-end wrapper. Without `--flash` it performs the safe
build, L1 validation, package, independent decode, and package-integrity gate:

```bash
<skill-dir>/scripts/full_flow.sh \
  --workspace <openvela-workspace> \
  --worktree <feature-worktree> \
  --jobs 12
```

The wrapper derives one stable slot per worktree under
`cmake_out/bk7258-worktrees/`. Its `build/cp` and optional `build/ap` directories
are reused for normal Vela incremental builds, and its `package` directory is
safely replaced on each successful package run. A binding file ties the slot to
the canonical workspace/worktree paths, so another worktree cannot reuse it.
If a component defconfig changes, only that component's generated build cache
is recreated. Use `--fresh` to deliberately recreate this worktree's generated
build cache. Use `--slot NAME` only to choose a stable human-readable slot.

To flash, rerun in an interactive terminal and explicitly add `--flash`:

```bash
<skill-dir>/scripts/full_flow.sh \
  --workspace <openvela-workspace> \
  --worktree <feature-worktree> \
  --flash --device /dev/ttyUSB0
```

To flash an existing verified package without rebuilding or requiring a
workspace/worktree, give the image and the board tools directory explicitly:

```bash
<skill-dir>/scripts/full_flow.sh \
  --image /absolute/path/to/all-app.bin \
  --tools-dir /absolute/path/to/board/bk7258-devkit/tools \
  --flash --device /dev/ttyUSB0
```

Image-only mode requires `manifest.json` and `decode-report.json` next to the
image. It runs the same independent integrity gate and automatic flash wrapper
but skips build/package. `--worktree <feature-worktree>` may replace
`--tools-dir`; the wrapper then derives `board/bk7258-devkit/tools` from that
worktree.

Flashing is destructive and must use an interactive terminal. The PTY wrapper
streams the loader output without buffering and drives the reset itself: once
the loader prints `connect success`, the wrapper opens the same serial device
as a second writer and injects `reboot bootloader` into the running NSH
console. Target firmware carrying the bootloader-reset patch
(`feature/bk7258-bootloader-reset`, `board_reset`
`ENTER_BOOTLOADER` via AON WDT) then performs a chip-level reset with the
vendor warm-jump tag cleared and the reset reason recorded as watchdog, so
the BootROM runs the cold chain and BL2 opens the download listen window
that the already-polling loader catches by itself -- no manual reset.
`Gotten Bus...` produces the handshake-success banner. If the automatic
reset does not engage within a few seconds (firmware without the patch, a
hung console), the wrapper retries once and then falls back to bell-and-
prompt manual resets, numbered 1, 2, ...; press reset on each prompt and
stop after the success banner. Never press reset after `Begin EraseFlash`,
and never type into the terminal during the automatic phase.

The public workflow assumes a trusted, current-user-owned workspace and Git
worktree. It does not defend against malicious processes running as the same
Unix user, SIGKILL, power loss, or tools that ignore its mapping lock. It never
runs worktree scripts through `sudo` and refuses to
run as root. Give the normal user access to the serial device through the
platform's serial-device group (commonly `dialout`). Before writing, the
wrapper verifies the audited `bk_loader` SHA-256, prints the complete image
SHA-256. The explicit `--flash` flag is the authorization switch. The agent
must still announce the target device and complete image hash in commentary
immediately before launching it.

When an agent launches the flash stage for the user, it must first announce in
commentary the target device, the complete image SHA-256, and that the wrapper
injects `reboot bootloader` automatically (manual-reset fallback prompts
appear only if the auto reset does not engage), then run the command with
interactive terminal support. Never launch `--flash` in the background,
through redirected output, or in a non-interactive shell. Keep the turn open
until `Writing Flash OK` or a clear failure is reported.

The existing board scripts remain the authority: `bk7258-package.sh` must
produce `decode pass`, and `bk7258-flash.sh` must reproduce the report, validate
all hashes, save the loader log, and find `Writing Flash OK`.

## Scope

This workflow is for a BK7258 team-repository worktree whose sources are
linked into the parent OpenVela workspace. The parent workspace is the
directory containing both `build.sh` and `nuttx/`; it is not the team-repository
checkout and not the worktree directory itself.

Never build a BK7258 worktree by passing `board/bk7258-devkit/configs/cp` to
`build.sh`. That path is valid for repository-local Python tools, but
`build.sh`/`lunch` resolves board configs through the manifest path under
`vendor/beken/boards/...`.

## 1. Establish the worktree mapping

For normal worktree builds, use the bundled wrapper; it serializes access to
the shared mapping and restores both links on exit:

```bash
<skill-dir>/scripts/build_worktree.sh \
  --workspace <openvela-workspace> \
  --worktree <feature-worktree> \
  --component cp \
  --jobs 12
```

Use `--component ap` for AP. Use `--output /absolute/output/path` only for an
isolated build whose artifacts will be passed explicitly to packaging.

From the parent OpenVela workspace, verify the mapped paths:

```bash
readlink -f vendor/beken/chips/bk7258
readlink -f vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit
```

For a feature worktree, both targets must resolve into that worktree:

```text
<worktree>/chips/bk7258
<worktree>/board/bk7258-devkit
```

If they point at another checkout, stop and resolve the mapping before
building. In a shared workspace, changing symlinks is visible to other
processes. Prefer a serialized build, save both original link targets, and
restore them in a shell `trap` even when the build fails. Do not delete the
symlink targets or use a broad recursive cleanup.

The project manifest is the source of truth for the normal mapping. The build
tree consumes the mapped `vendor/` paths, while packaging scripts may be run
from the worktree because they locate the workspace by the `build.sh` and
`nuttx/` markers.

## 2. Configure and build CP/AP

Run from the parent workspace. Use the mapped path and keep the trailing slash:

```bash
./build.sh vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit/configs/cp/ --cmake -j12
./build.sh vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit/configs/ap/ --cmake -j12
```

For a CP-only or Wi-Fi-disabled platform change, the first command is the
minimum build. Confirm the generated `.config` does not enable Wi-Fi/WPA when
the acceptance requires a normal CP configuration with Wi-Fi disabled.

`build.sh` derives output names from the board/config selection. Do not add a
random `-b` directory unless the task explicitly needs isolation:

```text
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/bk7258/app.bin
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/bk7258/nuttx.elf
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/bk7258/l1-validation.json
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_ap/bk7258_ap/app1.bin
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_ap/bk7258_ap/l1-validation.json
```

The normal build command supplies the project environment and compiler wrapper.
Direct `cmake --build` can fail with missing `ccache` or stale source paths and
is not equivalent evidence.

## 3. Package and independently decode

The default flow builds and packages the real CP plus OpenVela AP AMP image.
The bundled AP placeholder is recovery-only and must be selected explicitly
with `--placeholder`; it is expected to fail CPU1 AP release validation at
runtime.

For the repository-bundled recovery package, the project wrapper is the
preferred path:

```bash
<worktree>/board/bk7258-devkit/tools/bk7258-package.sh
```

It reads the CP/AP outputs, selects the real OpenVela AP profile, and runs the
independent decoder. The wrapper must print `decode       pass` before an image
is considered valid.

The default package slot intentionally replaces its previous package after the
new CP/AP build and L1 validation pass. `all-app.bin`, `manifest.json`, and
`decode-report.json` remain bound and are verified together before flashing.
Copy that trio elsewhere explicitly when a run must be preserved as historical
hardware evidence.

The package wrapper validates both L1 reports, invokes the container packer,
and independently decodes the final linear-CRC image. Do not flash `app.bin`
or `app1.bin` directly.

## 4. Offline regression checks

Run from the parent workspace or pass paths explicitly:

```bash
python3 <worktree>/board/bk7258-devkit/tests/test_bk7258_bundled_packaging.py
```

The decoder must produce the same report for relative and absolute input paths.
The report normalizes `image.path` with `Path.resolve()`; do not regress this
to the caller's spelling of the path, because evidence hashes and reports must
be stable across invocation directories.

For the vendor-input profile, first validate the machine-local input file and
then run the profile/package test described in
`board/bk7258-devkit/packaging/README.md`. Never invent vendor input paths or
copy credentials into the repository.

## 5. Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `No config file found at` | `build.sh` received `board/...` instead of mapped `vendor/...` path, or the path lacks the expected config directory | Run from the parent workspace with `vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit/configs/cp/` or `ap/` and verify `readlink -f` |
| Early `grep: dor/.../defconfig: No such file` followed by a valid `lunch`, build, and L1 pass | `build.sh` has a non-fatal path-slicing check before `lunch` for full mapped paths | Judge the final command result; do not treat this line alone as failure. A later `No config file found at` or nonzero build result is still a real failure |
| Output builds the wrong source checkout | Shared `vendor/` symlink points at another worktree | Save/replace the two BK7258 links for the build, serialize the operation, and restore them with a trap |
| Image size/config unexpectedly changes while build still passes | A standard CMake output directory retained another worktree's `.config` | Use `full_flow.sh`; its binding prevents cross-worktree cache reuse, and defconfig changes rebuild only the affected component slot |
| `ccache: not found` from direct CMake | Bypassed the environment setup used by `build.sh` | Re-run through `./build.sh ... --cmake` |
| CP image not found during packaging | CP build was not successful or used a custom output directory | Check `cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/bk7258/app.bin`, its L1 report, and pass `--cp-app-bin` when using `-b` |
| Decoder report differs by working directory | Decoder received relative input and stored it verbatim | Use the current decoder that resolves `args.image`; run the path-stability regression |
| Too many generated directories | A one-shot workflow was used instead of the stable bound slot | Use the default `full_flow.sh`; it incrementally reuses one build slot and replaces one package slot per worktree |
| `Getting Bus...` keeps printing but `Gotten Bus...` never appears, then the manual-reset banner shows up | The automatic `reboot bootloader` did not engage: target firmware lacks the bootloader-reset patch, its console was hung, or the injection window was missed | Press reset on each numbered bell/banner from `notify_flash.py`; stop resetting after `Gotten Bus...`. Deploy `feature/bk7258-bootloader-reset` firmware for the automatic path |
| No reset prompt and no auto-reset banner are visible | Flash was launched without a PTY or through a buffered pipe | Run `full_flow.sh --flash` in an interactive terminal; do not redirect loader stdout |
| `GetBus fail` or `LinkCheck Timeout` | Reset timing, USB, downloader mode, or a busy serial port prevented handshake; Flash has not been erased yet | Close serial monitors and rerun the interactive flash stage |
| Flash refuses root or reports serial permission denied | Public workflow does not execute mutable worktree code as root | Add the user to the serial-device group, re-login, and run without `sudo` |
| Loader SHA-256 mismatch | The bundled proprietary loader differs from the audited repository version | Stop; review the binary change and update the pinned hash only through code review |

## Acceptance boundary

A successful host build proves compilation and L1 image validation only. A
passing package/decode proves the linear-CRC container contract. Hardware IRQ,
register readback, GPIO waveform, cold boot, and UART behavior require separate
target evidence and must not be claimed from this workflow alone.

6	# BK7258 真机 UI 测试（ai_agent_ui）
7	
8	真机屏幕验证 ai_agent UI 各页面/状态的标准流程与指令。目标是**复用**而非每次重新摸索——读本文即接续上次进度，别从零踩坑。
9	
10	## 背景（路 B 架构，必读）
11	
12	- BK7258 双核：**CP(CPU0) 拥有 LCD/LVGL/FPU**，**AP(CPU1) 跑 agent/LLM/voice**。
13	- 真机 UI 由 CP 侧 builtin **`ai_agent_ui`** 渲染（`packages/ai_agent/src/ui_cp/cp_ui_main.c`），自起 LVGL + chat screen + pet_status_view + particle_flow_view。
14	- AP→CP 的 UI 走 RPMsg（ui_rpmsg_client → ui_rpmsg_server），但**真机上 AP agent 没跑**，所以测试走 **CP 本地调试菜单**（cp_ui_main.c 里加的 help/page/pet/ptt/say/sayc/user/demo）。
15	- 串口：CP NSH 控制台 = **/dev/ttyUSB0**（CH340，115200）；AP 日志 = /dev/ttyACM1（921600）。
16	
17	## 测试前准备
18	
19	1. **烧录**含调试菜单的最新 CP 镜像（流程见 bk7258-worktree-build）。两条硬约束：
20	   - 当前固件**不含 bootloader-reset patch**：notify_flash.py 的自动 `reboot bootloader` 不生效，必须在 `Getting Bus...` 窗口**手动按 RESET 键（K1，接 CEN，别按 S1/S2/S3）**，直到 `Gotten Bus` / `Writing Flash OK`。
21	   - 烧录前必须先 `tmux kill-session -t diag` 关掉 picocom（释放 ttyUSB0）。
22	2. 开串口：`tmux new-session -d -s diag 'picocom /dev/ttyUSB0 -b 115200 --imap lfcrlf'`。
23	3. 确认 NSH 可交互：发回车看到 `nsh>`；`help` 里 Builtin Apps 应含 `ai_agent_ui`。
24	
25	## 启动 UI
26	
27	前台启动（调试菜单只在**前台**能收到命令）：
28	
29	```
30	ai_agent_ui
31	```
32	
33	启动成功判据（syslog）：`[pet_view] init OK` / `[particle_view] init OK` / `[lvgl_ui] started` / `[ai_agent_ui] UI up; LVGL thread running`。此刻屏幕 = pet 首屏（idle 绿呼吸环）。
34	
35	> 烧录后板子自动重启，NSH 干净起来，`ai_agent_ui` **不会自动启动**，必须手动敲。若前台启动后 NSH prompt 消失、命令无回显，是它前台占了 stdin——正常。
36	
37	## 调试命令表
38	
39	| 命令 | 作用 |
40	|---|---|
41	| `help` | 打印命令表 |
42	| `show` / `chat` | 切聊天气泡屏 |
43	| `page 0` | pet 状态环首屏 |
44	| `page 1` | particle 粒子流页 |
45	| `pet 0..5` | 设置 pet 状态（同时镜像到 particle）：0=idle绿 1=listening青 2=thinking蓝 3=executing橙 4=waiting黄 5=error红 |
46	| `ptype 0..4` | 切换像素宠物：0=白猫 1=绿青蛙 2=黑猫 3=棕狗 4=粉猪（越界回猫，下一帧状态更新即生效） |
47	| `ptt 0/1/2` | PTT 状态：0=idle 1=录音中 2=识别中 |
48	| `user <text>` | 用户右对齐蓝气泡（无 TTS） |
49	| `say <text>` | Agent 气泡（自动分类色条） |
50	| `sayc <hex> <text>` | Agent 气泡 + 指定色条颜色 |
51	| `demo` | 一键轮转 pet 0-5 → particle 0-5 → chat + 4 色条，最后回 pet idle |
52	| `quit` | 退出 UI 回 NSH（Ctrl-C 无效，前台 builtin 收不到 SIGINT） |
53	
54	### 色条色值（`sayc` 第二个参数）
55	
56	| 分类 | 色值 |
57	|---|---|
58	| 蓝 structured | `0x3a7bd5` |
59	| 绿 conclusion | `0x4caf50` |
60	| 橙 jira | `0xff9800` |
61	| 灰 plain | `0x9e9e9e` |
62	
63	## 踩坑清单（必读，每条都踩过）
64	
65	1. **烧录自动复位（已含 patch，但 ai_agent_ui 会污染注入）**：2026-10-14 起固件已含 bootloader-reset patch，`notify_flash.py` 自动注入 `reboot bootloader` **零人工**生效（两次实测 `Gotten Bus`→`Writing Flash OK`）。但**烧录前必须确保 ai_agent_ui 没在前台/后台跑**——它持续打 `[lv_nuttx_lcd] flush #N` 日志刷屏，会污染注入字节（`reboot bootloader` 到 NSH 变乱码 `command not found`），导致 `GetBus fail`。正确顺序：`kill -9 <ai_agent_ui pid>`（`ps` 里 COMMAND=ai_agent_ui 的 Task pid）→ 确认 NSH 干净 → 再烧。若已 GetBus fail，板子其实没被擦，重试前先 ps 确认无 ai_agent_ui。
66	2. **TX 掉线**：若发命令无任何回显、只有板子→host 的日志（idle rotate/adc release）在滚，是 host→board TX 掉线。软重插 CH340（`echo 0/1 > /sys/bus/usb/devices/1-2/authorized`）**无效**，要物理拔插 USB 断电。烧录脚本的 `do_reset_signal` 也会顺带复位板子恢复串口。
67	3. **`show` 不重置 idle 让位**：`lvgl_ui_channel_show` 不调用 `pet_idle_reset`。若上次消息已超 8s，`show` 后约 1s 内就被 idle 切回 pet。**正确做法：直接发气泡（user/say/sayc），不手动 show**；气泡经 async 添加时才重置 idle tick（`chat_view_add_message_async_cb` 内 `pet_idle_reset()`）。
68	4. **气泡添加不打日志**：`chat_view_add_message` 静默，无 syslog。判断气泡是否生效**看屏幕**，别靠日志。`help`/`pet` 有日志；`show`/`user`/`say` 通常没有（除非触发 `loading chat screen`）。
69	5. **idle 让位/轮转**：chat 屏空闲 8s 自动回 pet（`PET_IDLE_YIELD_MS=8000`）；idle 时 pet↔particle 每 10s 轮转（`ROTATE_INTERVAL_MS=10000`）。发气泡会暂停轮转。
70	6. **异步时序**：所有 UI 命令经 `lv_async_call` 调度到 LVGL 线程执行，日志有延迟。`demo` 的 chat 部分是异步排队，demo 主循环立即返回，chat 屏在 demo 结束后才真正 load（`set_page(0)` 先切回 pet，随后 chat 异步 load 又抢前台）。
71	7. **flush 慢（根因已定位）**：新镜像 flush **1.9~9.8 flush/s** 是 defconfig `CONFIG_BK7258_LCD1_SPI_BITBANG=y`（bit-bang 软件翻转 GPIO，天然慢）所致，**不是**增量构建带偏，与 cp_ui_main.c 改动无关；旧镜像 145/s 是 HW SPI。回快档：defconfig 去 `CONFIG_BK7258_LCD1_SPI_BITBANG`、改 `CONFIG_BK7258_LCD1_SPI_HW=y`（bk7258_spi_hw.c 已存在，第 60 行 `#ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_LCD1_SPI_HW`），再刷 build-dir defconfig + 增量构建。`rate:` 日志判据：~145=HW SPI 正常，~2~10=bit-bang。**2026-10-14 现状**：已切回 HW SPI+`CONFIG_SPI=y`，宠物首屏 97×97 精灵区域实测 **19.7 flush/s**（每 flush ~17ms、约 1 MB/s≈8Mbps SPI 吞吐）；对像素猫脸的慢动画（呼吸/眨眼/上视下视/抖动）已够流畅，未深挖 SPI 时钟上探（145/s 是更高时钟或更小区域的历史数据）。
72	8. **中文经串口发送**：`tmux send-keys -t diag 'sayc 0x4caf50 值得合入，建议采纳' Enter` 中文可正常传入（UTF-8），picocom `--imap lfcrlf` 不影响。
73	
74	## 验证成功判据
75	
76	- 屏幕按命令在 pet / particle / chat 三页之间切换。
77	- pet 6 状态颜色/形态变化可见（绿/青/蓝/橙/黄/红）。
78	- chat 屏显示 1 条 user 右对齐蓝气泡 + 4 条色条 Agent 卡片（蓝/绿/橙/灰）。
79	- 日志 `[lv_nuttx_lcd] flush rc=0`（无渲染报错）。
80	
81	## 测试后收尾
82	
83	- `quit` 退出 ai_agent_ui 回 NSH（或直接 `tmux kill-session -t diag` 断串口）。
84

54	 *     period 0xA).

56	 * The CP firmware runs from the 0x280xxxxx SRAM window, so the DTCM tag

58	 */

60	#define BK7258_AON_PMU_BASE      0x44000000ul
61	#define BK7258_AON_PMU_R0_ADDR   (BK7258_AON_PMU_BASE + (0x0 << 2))
62	#define BK7258_AON_PMU_R2_ADDR   (BK7258_AON_PMU_BASE + (0x2 << 2))
63	#define BK7258_AON_PMU_R41_ADDR  (BK7258_AON_PMU_BASE + (0x41 << 2))
64	#define BK7258_AON_WDT_BASE      0x44000600ul
65	#define BK7258_REBOOT_TAG_ADDR   0x20003ff8ul
66	
67	/* Vendor reset_reason.h REBOOT_TAG_REQ: a set tag makes the BootROM warm
68	 * fast-jump into the running app's startup trampoline (planned reboot);
69	 * a cleared tag plus a WATCHDOG reason runs the full cold chain so BL2
70	 * opens the download window. */
71	
72	#define BK7258_REBOOT_TAG_REQ    0xaa55aa55ul
73

75	 * accessors, so use plain volatile pointer access here. */
76	
77	static inline uint32_t bk7258_reg_rd(uintptr_t addr)
78	{
79	  return *(volatile uint32_t *)addr;
80	}
81	
82	static inline void bk7258_reg_wr(uintptr_t addr, uint32_t value)
83	{
84	  *(volatile uint32_t *)addr = value;
85	}

88	/****************************************************************************
89	 * Name: bk7258_aon_wdt_chip_reset
90	 *
91	 * Description:
92	 *   Force a chip-level reset through the AON WDT.  Mirrors
93	 *   wdt_hal_force_reboot(); the only difference between a planned reboot
94	 *   and a bootloader entry is the warm tag and the recorded reset reason.
95	 *
96	 *   SYSRESETREQ (up_systemreset) is not usable on this AMP part: it only
97	 *   resets CPU0 and leaves CPU1/RPTUN/shared-device state behind, which
98	 *   wedges the reboot chain ("Rptun driver reset remote ap" is the last
99	 *   line).  The AON WDT resets the device at the PMU level like the reset
100	 *   button, so both cores restart cleanly.  (dev 16e61a3, hand-merged
101	 *   with the AP bootloader-request path.)
102	 *
103	 *   The RPTUN reboot notifier has already reset the AP by the time the
104	 *   reboot chain reaches board_reset(); this chip reset covers CPU1 again
105	 *   regardless, and the normal bring-up re-releases it afterwards.
106	 *
107	 ****************************************************************************/
108	
109	static void bk7258_aon_wdt_chip_reset(bool enter_bootloader)
110	{
111	  uint32_t val;
112	
113	  if (enter_bootloader)
114	    {
115	      /* Clear the vendor warm fast-jump tag and record
116	       * RESET_SOURCE_WATCHDOG (0x2): BootROM runs the full cold chain and
117	       * BL2 opens the serial download handshake window.  The AON PMU
118	       * survives the chip reset, so the reason written here is what the
119	       * ROM/BL2 reads to classify the next boot; without it the ROM keeps
120	       * skipping BL2 even though the tag is gone.  AP reason lives in R0
121	       * bits[24:30] (7 bits), CP reason in bits[4:11] (8 bits). */
122	
123	      bk7258_reg_wr(BK7258_REBOOT_TAG_ADDR, 0ul);
124	
125	      val = bk7258_reg_rd(BK7258_AON_PMU_R0_ADDR);
126	      val &= ~((0x7ful << 24) | (0xfful << 4));
127	      val |= (0x2ul << 24) | (0x2ul << 4);
128	      bk7258_reg_wr(BK7258_AON_PMU_R0_ADDR, val);
129	    }
130	  else
131	    {
132	      /* Vendor planned reboot: set the warm tag so the BootROM fast-jumps
133	       * back into the startup trampoline.  The PMU-level reset is what
134	       * makes this path safe on AMP where SYSRESETREQ is not. */
135	
136	      bk7258_reg_wr(BK7258_REBOOT_TAG_ADDR, BK7258_REBOOT_TAG_REQ);
137	    }
138	
139	  /* Vendor aon_pmu_drv_wdt_change_not_rosc_clk(): select clk_DIVD as the
140	   * WDT LPO source so the emergency period bites deterministically. */
141	
142	  val = bk7258_reg_rd(BK7258_AON_PMU_R41_ADDR);
143	  val &= ~0x3ul;
144	  bk7258_reg_wr(BK7258_AON_PMU_R41_ADDR, val);
145	
146	  /* Vendor aon_pmu_hal_wdt_rst_dev_enable(): gate the AON WDT through to
147	   * the PMU reset line, keeping every other R2 bit unchanged. */
148	
149	  val = bk7258_reg_rd(BK7258_AON_PMU_R2_ADDR);
150	  val &= ~0x3ful;
151	  val |= 0x26ul;
152	  bk7258_reg_wr(BK7258_AON_PMU_R2_ADDR, val);
153	
154	  /* Vendor wdt_hal_force_reboot(): arm the AON WDT.  The control word
155	   * carries the key in bits[23:16] and the period in the low bits; two
156	   * writes with different keys are required for the value to latch. */
157	
158	  bk7258_reg_wr(BK7258_AON_WDT_BASE, 0x5a000aul);
159	  bk7258_reg_wr(BK7258_AON_WDT_BASE, 0xa5000aul);
160	
161	  /* The reset comes from the PMU, not from here. */
162	
163	  for (; ; );
164	}

# BK7258 Worktree Build

## Complete workflow

Prefer the bundled end-to-end wrapper. Without `--flash` it performs the safe
build, L1 validation, package, independent decode, and package-integrity gate:

```bash
<skill-dir>/scripts/full_flow.sh \
  --workspace <openvela-workspace> \
  --worktree <feature-worktree> \
  --jobs 12
```

The wrapper derives one stable slot per worktree under
`cmake_out/bk7258-worktrees/`. Its `build/cp` and optional `build/ap` directories
are reused for normal Vela incremental builds, and its `package` directory is
safely replaced on each successful package run. A binding file ties the slot to
the canonical workspace/worktree paths, so another worktree cannot reuse it.
If a component defconfig changes, only that component's generated build cache
is recreated. Use `--fresh` to deliberately recreate this worktree's generated
build cache. Use `--slot NAME` only to choose a stable human-readable slot.

To flash, rerun in an interactive terminal and explicitly add `--flash`:

```bash
<skill-dir>/scripts/full_flow.sh \
  --workspace <openvela-workspace> \
  --worktree <feature-worktree> \
  --flash --device /dev/ttyUSB0
```

To flash an existing verified package without rebuilding or requiring a
workspace/worktree, give the image and the board tools directory explicitly:

```bash
<skill-dir>/scripts/full_flow.sh \
  --image /absolute/path/to/all-app.bin \
  --tools-dir /absolute/path/to/board/bk7258-devkit/tools \
  --flash --device /dev/ttyUSB0
```

Image-only mode requires `manifest.json` and `decode-report.json` next to the
image. It runs the same independent integrity gate and automatic flash wrapper
but skips build/package. `--worktree <feature-worktree>` may replace
`--tools-dir`; the wrapper then derives `board/bk7258-devkit/tools` from that
worktree.

Flashing is destructive and must use an interactive terminal. The PTY wrapper
streams the loader output without buffering and drives the reset itself: once
the loader prints `connect success`, the wrapper opens the same serial device
as a second writer and injects `reboot bootloader` into the running NSH
console. Target firmware carrying the bootloader-reset patch
(`feature/bk7258-bootloader-reset`, `board_reset`
`ENTER_BOOTLOADER` via AON WDT) then performs a chip-level reset with the
vendor warm-jump tag cleared and the reset reason recorded as watchdog, so
the BootROM runs the cold chain and BL2 opens the download listen window
that the already-polling loader catches by itself -- no manual reset.
`Gotten Bus...` produces the handshake-success banner. If the automatic
reset does not engage within a few seconds (firmware without the patch, a
hung console), the wrapper retries once and then falls back to bell-and-
prompt manual resets, numbered 1, 2, ...; press reset on each prompt and
stop after the success banner. Never press reset after `Begin EraseFlash`,
and never type into the terminal during the automatic phase.

The public workflow assumes a trusted, current-user-owned workspace and Git
worktree. It does not defend against malicious processes running as the same
Unix user, SIGKILL, power loss, or tools that ignore its mapping lock. It never
runs worktree scripts through `sudo` and refuses to
run as root. Give the normal user access to the serial device through the
platform's serial-device group (commonly `dialout`). Before writing, the
wrapper verifies the audited `bk_loader` SHA-256, prints the complete image
SHA-256. The explicit `--flash` flag is the authorization switch. The agent
must still announce the target device and complete image hash in commentary
immediately before launching it.

When an agent launches the flash stage for the user, it must first announce in
commentary the target device, the complete image SHA-256, and that the wrapper
injects `reboot bootloader` automatically (manual-reset fallback prompts
appear only if the auto reset does not engage), then run the command with
interactive terminal support. Never launch `--flash` in the background,
through redirected output, or in a non-interactive shell. Keep the turn open
until `Writing Flash OK` or a clear failure is reported.

The existing board scripts remain the authority: `bk7258-package.sh` must
produce `decode pass`, and `bk7258-flash.sh` must reproduce the report, validate
all hashes, save the loader log, and find `Writing Flash OK`.

## Scope

This workflow is for a BK7258 team-repository worktree whose sources are
linked into the parent OpenVela workspace. The parent workspace is the
directory containing both `build.sh` and `nuttx/`; it is not the team-repository
checkout and not the worktree directory itself.

Never build a BK7258 worktree by passing `board/bk7258-devkit/configs/cp` to
`build.sh`. That path is valid for repository-local Python tools, but
`build.sh`/`lunch` resolves board configs through the manifest path under
`vendor/beken/boards/...`.

## 1. Establish the worktree mapping

For normal worktree builds, use the bundled wrapper; it serializes access to
the shared mapping and restores both links on exit:

```bash
<skill-dir>/scripts/build_worktree.sh \
  --workspace <openvela-workspace> \
  --worktree <feature-worktree> \
  --component cp \
  --jobs 12
```

Use `--component ap` for AP. Use `--output /absolute/output/path` only for an
isolated build whose artifacts will be passed explicitly to packaging.

From the parent OpenVela workspace, verify the mapped paths:

```bash
readlink -f vendor/beken/chips/bk7258
readlink -f vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit
```

For a feature worktree, both targets must resolve into that worktree:

```text
<worktree>/chips/bk7258
<worktree>/board/bk7258-devkit
```

If they point at another checkout, stop and resolve the mapping before
building. In a shared workspace, changing symlinks is visible to other
processes. Prefer a serialized build, save both original link targets, and
restore them in a shell `trap` even when the build fails. Do not delete the
symlink targets or use a broad recursive cleanup.

The project manifest is the source of truth for the normal mapping. The build
tree consumes the mapped `vendor/` paths, while packaging scripts may be run
from the worktree because they locate the workspace by the `build.sh` and
`nuttx/` markers.

## 2. Configure and build CP/AP

Run from the parent workspace. Use the mapped path and keep the trailing slash:

```bash
./build.sh vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit/configs/cp/ --cmake -j12
./build.sh vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit/configs/ap/ --cmake -j12
```

For a CP-only or Wi-Fi-disabled platform change, the first command is the
minimum build. Confirm the generated `.config` does not enable Wi-Fi/WPA when
the acceptance requires a normal CP configuration with Wi-Fi disabled.

`build.sh` derives output names from the board/config selection. Do not add a
random `-b` directory unless the task explicitly needs isolation:

```text
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/bk7258/app.bin
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/bk7258/nuttx.elf
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/bk7258/l1-validation.json
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_ap/bk7258_ap/app1.bin
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_ap/bk7258_ap/l1-validation.json
```

The normal build command supplies the project environment and compiler wrapper.
Direct `cmake --build` can fail with missing `ccache` or stale source paths and
is not equivalent evidence.

## 3. Package and independently decode

The default flow builds and packages the real CP plus OpenVela AP AMP image.
The bundled AP placeholder is recovery-only and must be selected explicitly
with `--placeholder`; it is expected to fail CPU1 AP release validation at
runtime.

For the repository-bundled recovery package, the project wrapper is the
preferred path:

```bash
<worktree>/board/bk7258-devkit/tools/bk7258-package.sh
```

It reads the CP/AP outputs, selects the real OpenVela AP profile, and runs the
independent decoder. The wrapper must print `decode       pass` before an image
is considered valid.

The default package slot intentionally replaces its previous package after the
new CP/AP build and L1 validation pass. `all-app.bin`, `manifest.json`, and
`decode-report.json` remain bound and are verified together before flashing.
Copy that trio elsewhere explicitly when a run must be preserved as historical
hardware evidence.

The package wrapper validates both L1 reports, invokes the container packer,
and independently decodes the final linear-CRC image. Do not flash `app.bin`
or `app1.bin` directly.

## 4. Offline regression checks

Run from the parent workspace or pass paths explicitly:

```bash
python3 <worktree>/board/bk7258-devkit/tests/test_bk7258_bundled_packaging.py
```

The decoder must produce the same report for relative and absolute input paths.
The report normalizes `image.path` with `Path.resolve()`; do not regress this

For the vendor-input profile, first validate the machine-local input file and
then run the profile/package test described in
`board/bk7258-devkit/packaging/README.md`. Never invent vendor input paths or

## 5. Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `No config file found at` | `build.sh` received `board/...` instead of mapped `vendor/...` path, or the path lacks the expected config directory | Run from the parent workspace with `vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit/configs/cp/` or `ap/` and verify `readlink -f` |
| Early `grep: dor/.../defconfig: No such file` followed by a valid `lunch`, build, and L1 pass | `build.sh` has a non-fatal path-slicing check before `lunch` for full mapped paths | Judge the final command result; do not treat this line alone as failure. A later `No config file found at` or nonzero build result is still a real failure |
| Output builds the wrong source checkout | Shared `vendor/` symlink points at another worktree | Save/replace the two BK7258 links for the build, serialize the operation, and restore them with a trap |
| Image size/config unexpectedly changes while build still passes | A standard CMake output directory retained another worktree's `.config` | Use `full_flow.sh`; its binding prevents cross-worktree cache reuse, and defconfig changes rebuild only the affected component slot |
| `ccache: not found` from direct CMake | Bypassed the environment setup used by `build.sh` | Re-run through `./build.sh ... --cmake` |
| CP image not found during packaging | CP build was not successful or used a custom output directory | Check `cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/bk7258/app.bin`, its L1 report, and pass `--cp-app-bin` when using `-b` |
| Decoder report differs by working directory | Decoder received relative input and stored it verbatim | Use the current decoder that resolves `args.image`; run the path-stability regression |
| Too many generated directories | A one-shot workflow was used instead of the stable bound slot | Use the default `full_flow.sh`; it incrementally reuses one build slot and replaces one package slot per worktree |
| `Getting Bus...` keeps printing but `Gotten Bus...` never appears, then the manual-reset banner shows up | The automatic `reboot bootloader` did not engage: target firmware lacks the bootloader-reset patch, its console was hung, or the injection window was missed | Press reset on each numbered bell/banner from `notify_flash.py`; stop resetting after `Gotten Bus...`. Deploy `feature/bk7258-bootloader-reset` firmware for the automatic path |
| No reset prompt and no auto-reset banner are visible | Flash was launched without a PTY or through a buffered pipe | Run `full_flow.sh --flash` in an interactive terminal; do not redirect loader stdout |
| `GetBus fail` or `LinkCheck Timeout` | Reset timing, USB, downloader mode, or a busy serial port prevented handshake; Flash has not been erased yet | Close serial monitors and rerun the interactive flash stage |
| Flash refuses root or reports serial permission denied | Public workflow does not execute mutable worktree code as root | Add the user to the serial-device group, re-login, and run without `sudo` |
| Loader SHA-256 mismatch | The bundled proprietary loader differs from the audited repository version | Stop; review the binary change and update the pinned hash only through code review |

A successful host build proves compilation and L1 image validation only. A
passing package/decode proves the linear-CRC container contract. Hardware IRQ,
register readback, GPIO waveform, cold boot, and UART behavior require separate
target evidence and must not be claimed from this workflow alone.

```
ai_agent          # 启动,等 boot 到 P5,出现 vela> 提示符
```

175	    }

- `LV_NUTTX_LCD_DOUBLE_BUFFER` → `LV_NUTTX_LCD_BUFFER_COUNT=2` (FULL render mode, double full-screen buffer)
- `LV_NUTTX_LCD_CUSTOM_BUFFER` → `LV_NUTTX_LCD_BUFFER_COUNT=0` (PARTIAL render mode, strip buffer of size LV_NUTTX_LCD_BUFFER_SIZE)

```c
#if LV_NUTTX_LCD_BUFFER_COUNT > 0
    uint32_t buf_size = hor_res * ver_res * px_size;
    lv_display_render_mode_t render_mode = LV_DISPLAY_RENDER_MODE_FULL;
#else

    lv_display_render_mode_t render_mode = LV_DISPLAY_RENDER_MODE_PARTIAL;

```

So:
- `BUFFER_COUNT > 0` (1 or 2) → FULL mode, full-screen buffer(s). This is what's active (DOUBLE_BUFFER → count=2).
- `BUFFER_COUNT == 0` → PARTIAL mode, strip buffer of `LV_NUTTX_LCD_BUFFER_SIZE` lines.

The fix for the white sweep: switch from FULL (double buffer) to PARTIAL (custom buffer, count=0), with a reasonable `LV_NUTTX_LCD_BUFFER_SIZE` (e.g., 20-40 lines). Then LVGL only renders + flushes dirty regions.

Actually, let me reconsider whether partial rendering is even viable on this panel. The JD9853 panel + `bk7258_spi_hw.c` putarea. The `lv_nuttx_lcd.c` flush_cb sends `lcd->area` (row_start/end, col_start/end) via `LCDDEVIO_PUTAREA`. ## 根因:「白底刷屏」不是转场,是持续整屏重刷

关键事实:

1. **屏幕背景本来就是近黑 `0x0F1011`**(`ui_palette.h`),所以「白底」不是 UI 画的白色,而是 **JD9853 面板整帧 GRAM 重写时的扫描白闪**。
2. **渐隐渐显转场其实已经写好了**:`pet_status_view.c` / `particle_flow_view.c` / `lvgl_ui_channel.c` 里所有切屏都已经是 `lv_screen_load_anim(..., LV_SCR_LOAD_ANIM_FADE_IN, SCREEN_FADE_MS)`。但它只作用于**切屏那一瞬间**。
3. **真正持续刷屏的来源**:AP defconfig 开了 `CONFIG_LV_NUTTX_LCD_DOUBLE_BUFFER=y` → 编译期 `LV_NUTTX_LCD_BUFFER_COUNT=2` → LVGL 进 `RENDER_MODE_FULL`。宠物呼吸/浮动、粒子流动这些**动画每一帧都把整块 240×296 全屏重绘并整帧推到 13MHz SPI**(~280ms/帧 ≈ 1.3 flush/s),于是每帧一次从上到下白闪。旧的 CP 时代用的是 partial 模式(只刷脏区 97×97,19.7 flush/s),所以没这个问题。

**把 AP 渲染模式从整屏(FULL)切回局部(PARTIAL)**,改 defconfig 两行:
- 去掉 `CONFIG_LV_NUTTX_LCD_DOUBLE_BUFFER=y`
- 加 `CONFIG_LV_NUTTX_LCD_CUSTOM_BUFFER=y`(+ `CONFIG_LV_NUTTX_LCD_BUFFER_SIZE=60`)

这是**配置开关,不动 flush/SPI 驱动代码**(`lv_nuttx_lcd.c` 本就两条路径都支持,`bk7258_lcd.c`/`jd9853.c` 的窗口写从未改)。效果:动画只刷移动的粒子/弧环/精灵的小脏区,不再整屏白扫;已有的渐隐渐显转场保留(切屏那一下仍淡入)。

```c
#ifdef CONFIG_AI_AGENT_STANDBY_UI
/* Standby dim clock: after STANDBY_TIMEOUT_MS with no user/agent activity and
 * the agent idle (state==IDLE), fade the foreground over to a dim digital
 * clock (standby_view).  Any real activity (message / PTT / state change /
 * page switch / approval / scroll) resets the countdown and wakes the clock
 * off, restoring the previous screen.  The idle pet↔particle auto-rotate does
 * NOT count as activity (it switches the views directly, not via set_page). */
#define STANDBY_TIMEOUT_MS 60000
static lv_timer_t *s_standby_timer = NULL;
static uint32_t    s_last_activity_tick = 0;

static void ui_activity_reset(void)
{
    s_last_activity_tick = lv_tick_get();
    if (standby_view_is_visible())
        standby_view_hide();   /* async fade back to the previous screen */
}

static void standby_timer_cb(lv_timer_t *t)
{
    (void)t;
    if (!s_state.initialized || !s_state.running) return;
    if (standby_view_is_visible()) return;
    /* A busy (non-idle) agent keeps postponing standby so the thinking /
     * executing animation is never interrupted mid-task. */
    if (s_last_pet_state != 0)
      {
        s_last_activity_tick = lv_tick_get();
        return;
      }
    if ((lv_tick_get() - s_last_activity_tick) >= STANDBY_TIMEOUT_MS)
      {
        syslog(LOG_INFO, "[%s] idle %ums → standby clock\n", TAG,
               STANDBY_TIMEOUT_MS);
        standby_view_show();
      }
}
#else
static void ui_activity_reset(void) {}
#endif
```

```c
static void rotate_timer_cb(lv_timer_t *t)
{
    (void)t;
    if (!s_state.initialized) return;
    if (s_state.screen_visible) return;        /* chat holds the foreground */
    if (s_state.approval_visible) return;      /* approval page holds it */
    if (s_last_pet_state != 0) return;         /* only idle rotates */
#ifdef CONFIG_AI_AGENT_STANDBY_UI
    if (standby_view_is_visible()) return;     /* standby clock holds it */
#endif
    uint32_t now = lv_tick_get();
    if ((now - s_rotate_last_switch_tick) < ROTATE_INTERVAL_MS) return;
    if (pet_status_view_is_visible())
      {
        /* Direct view switch (not set_page) so idle rotation never counts as
         * user activity and cannot postpone the standby clock. */
        pet_status_view_hide();
        particle_flow_view_show();
        syslog(LOG_INFO, "[%s] idle rotate → particle\n", TAG);
      }
    else if (particle_flow_view_is_visible())
      {
        particle_flow_view_hide();
        pet_status_view_show();
        syslog(LOG_INFO, "[%s] idle rotate → pet\n", TAG);
      }
    s_rotate_last_switch_tick = now;
}
```

thinking:
So `lv_font.h` line 227 has `LV_FONT_DECLARE(lv_font_montserrat_24)` (guarded by `#if LV_FONT_MONTSERRAT_24` presumably). And `lv_font.h` is included by `lvgl.h`. So including `<lvgl/lvgl.h>` (which the file already does) makes `lv_font_montserrat_24` available directly as `&lv_font_montserrat_24`. 

So no `LV_FONT_DECLARE` needed for montserrat — just use `&lv_font_montserrat_24`. But wait, there's the `LV_LVGL_H_INCLUDE_SIMPLE` macro and `LV_FONT_MONTSERRAT_24` guard. In NuttX, `CONFIG_LV_FONT_MONTSERRAT_24=y` translates to `LV_FONT_MONTSERRAT_24` being defined (probably via a generated config header `lv_conf.h` or a Kconfig→define mapping). Since defconfig has `CONFIG_LV_FONT_MONTSERRAT_24=y`, the symbol is compiled (the `.o` exists in the build dir per the find output: `cmake_out/.../lvgl.dir/lvgl/src/font/lv_font_montserrat_24.c.o`). So `lv_font_montserrat_24` is linked.

So in standby_view.c, I can just do `&lv_font_montserrat_24` directly after `#include <lvgl/lvgl.h>`. Good. No `LV_FONT_DECLARE(lv_font_montserrat_24)` needed (though adding it would also be harmless). To match the idiom used for miSans (app-owned font needs LV_FONT_DECLARE), I'll declare miSans via LV_FONT_DECLARE and use montserrat directly.

Now, the important finding about callers: `cp_ui_main.c` calls `lvgl_ui_channel_set_page` and `lvgl_ui_channel_set_pet_state` — but that's the DEAD CP path (UI_CP, not built on AP). On the AP (current target), the callers of `set_pet_state` are:
- `agent_main.c:438` (state 5 = error)
- `agent_loop.c:1557` (state 2 = thinking), `1578` (state 0 = idle)
- `ptt_button.c:195` (state 5)
- `nsh_commands.c:1303` (CLI set_pet)

And `set_page` callers on AP: `nsh_commands.c:1307` (CLI set_page). The `cp_ui_main.c` and `ui_rpmsg_server.c` are UI_CP/UI_RPMSG paths (not built on AP where UI is local).

Wait — actually, `agent_loop.c` calls `set_pet_state(2)` (thinking) and `(0)` (idle) during normal agent processing. This is CRITICAL: `set_pet_state(0)` (idle) is called whenever the agent returns to idle. This would call `ui_activity_reset()` each time!

Let me think about this carefully. The agent lifecycle:
- When user sends a message → agent goes thinking (state 2) → processing → idle (state 0).
- `agent_loop.c:1578` calls `set_pet_state(0)` when returning to idle.

If `set_pet_state` calls `ui_activity_reset()`, then EVERY agent response (which ends in idle) resets the activity tick. That's actually FINE and DESIRED: an agent response IS activity, and after it completes, the 60s countdown restarts. So standby would only trigger 60s after the last agent response/idle transition. That's correct behavior.

But wait — there's a subtlety. Is `set_pet_state(0)` called periodically even when nothing is happening? Let me check agent_loop.c around 1578. If there's an idle heartbeat that repeatedly calls `set_pet_state(0)`, it would prevent standby from ever triggering. Let me check.

Actually, `set_pet_state` already has the guard `if (state != s_last_pet_state)` at line 980. So calling `set_pet_state(0)` repeatedly when already idle does nothing (no rotate_idle_reset). But MY `ui_activity_reset()` call is placed BEFORE that guard (I put it right after the state-range check). So if `set_pet_state(0)` is called repeatedly while idle, `ui_activity_reset()` would be called repeatedly, preventing standby.

This is a real problem. I need to place `ui_activity_reset()` INSIDE the `if (state != s_last_pet_state)` guard, so that only a genuine state CHANGE resets activity. OR, more precisely, only reset activity when the state actually changes (a real lifecycle event).

Let me reconsider. The `set_pet_state` function:
```c
int lvgl_ui_channel_set_pet_state(int state)
{
    int rc = -ENOSYS;
    if (state < 0 || state > PET_STATE_ERROR) {
        return -EINVAL;
    }
    // ... set state on pet + particle views ...
    (void)rc;
    if (state != s_last_pet_state)
      {
        s_last_pet_state = state;
        rotate_idle_reset();
      }
    return rc;
}
```

If I put `ui_activity_reset()` inside the `if (state != s_last_pet_state)` block, then:
- A genuine state change (idle→thinking, thinking→idle, etc.) resets activity. ✓
- Repeated `set_pet_state(0)` while idle does nothing. ✓

That's the correct placement. So for `set_pet_state`, I should NOT add `ui_activity_reset()` at the top; instead add it inside the `if (state != s_last_pet_state)` block.

But wait — there's another subtlety. When the agent is idle and the user does nothing, does agent_loop call `set_pet_state(0)` at all? If it does (e.g., every heartbeat), even with the `state != s_last_pet_state` guard, it won't reset (because state is already 0). Good.

But also consider: when the agent goes idle after a response, `set_pet_state(0)` is called ONCE (transition from thinking→idle), resetting activity. After that, 60s of true idle → standby. Correct.

However, there's a deeper concern: `s_last_pet_state` is only updated when the state actually changes. But what about the transition idle→idle (no change)? Not relevant.

So the correct edit for `set_pet_state`:
```c
    if (state != s_last_pet_state)
      {
        s_last_pet_state = state;
        rotate_idle_reset();
        ui_activity_reset();   /* genuine lifecycle change = activity */
      }
```

Wait, but is a state change TO idle "activity"? When the agent finishes a task and goes idle, that's the moment after which the 60s idle countdown should begin. So resetting activity on idle transition is exactly right. And transitions to thinking/listening/executing are obviously activity.

But hold on — there's a subtlety with the standby timer itself. When standby is visible and the agent is idle, the standby_timer_cb checks `if (s_last_pet_state != 0) return;`. Since idle=0, it proceeds. Good.

But what if the agent autonomously does something (e.g., a cron/heartbeat) that triggers `set_pet_state(2)` (thinking) then back to `0`? Then standby would be postponed (activity reset), which is correct — the agent was actually doing something.

OK so the placement for set_pet_state is inside the guard.

Now, similar concern for `set_ptt`. `set_ptt` is called by ptt_button.c on button press/release. A button press is genuine activity. `set_ptt(LVGL_UI_PTT_IDLE)` is called on release. Is it called repeatedly while idle? No — only on actual button events. So putting `ui_activity_reset()` at the top of `set_ptt` is fine. But to be safe, should I also guard it? PTT events are edge-triggered (button press/release), not a continuous heartbeat. So top-of-function is fine. Actually, let me think: on button PRESS, set_ptt(RECORDING) is called; on RELEASE, set_ptt(IDLE). Each is a real activity. So resetting on each is correct (a button press keeps you awake). Good.

Now `show`, `send`, `send_ex`, `send_user`, `scroll`, `set_approval`, `clear_approval`, `set_page` — these are all user/agent-driven edge events, not continuous heartbeats. So top-of-function `ui_activity_reset()` is correct for all of them.

But wait — `send` and `send_user` also call `show()` internally. And I'm adding `ui_activity_reset()` to both `show` and `send`. Redundant but harmless.

Actually, let me reconsider `show`. Is `lvgl_ui_channel_show()` ever called in a loop/heartbeat? It's called from send/send_ex/send_user/scroll when `!screen_visible`, and from CLI `show`. Not a heartbeat. So fine.

Now, another important consideration: `agent_main.c:438` calls `set_pet_state(5)` (error state) — probably on some error event. That's activity. Fine.

Now let me also reconsider: the standby timer cb checks `s_last_pet_state != 0` to postpone. But what about `s_state.screen_visible` (chat visible) or `s_state.approval_visible`? When chat is visible (user is reading a response), should standby trigger? The requirement is "长时间没有操作" (no operation). If chat is showing a response and the user is idle, after 60s it should go standby. But if I don't check screen_visible, the standby will trigger while chat is visible. Is that desired?

The user said "如果长时间没有操作，自动进入待机界面UI" — after long no-operation, enter standby. So even if chat is showing (but no new operation), standby should eventually trigger. That's the whole point. So I should NOT skip when screen_visible.

BUT — there's a subtlety. The standby screen's `prev_screen` restore: if chat is visible when standby triggers, `standby_view_show` saves `prev_screen = lv_screen_active()` = chat screen. On wake, `standby_view_hide` restores chat. That works.

However, the rotate_timer_cb and pet_idle_timer_cb have their own logic. When chat is visible, `pet_idle_timer_cb` (the 8s yield) would normally yield chat back to pet after 8s idle. So actually, after an agent response, the chat screen auto-yields to pet after 8s (PET_IDLE_YIELD_MS). Then the pet/particle rotate takes over. So by the time 60s elapses, chat is likely already gone (yielded to pet), and standby triggers on the pet/particle screen. That's the natural flow.

But what if PET_IDLE_YIELD doesn't fire (e.g., chat stays visible because... hmm)? Let me check: `pet_idle_timer_cb` yields chat→pet after 8s of no chat message. So chat auto-dismisses. So standby will most likely trigger on the pet screen (or particle if rotating). Fine.

Actually, wait — there's a potential conflict. `pet_idle_timer_cb` (8s yield) and `rotate_timer_cb` (10s rotate) and `standby_timer_cb` (60s standby) all run at 1s period. When idle:
- t=0: last activity (agent went idle).
- t=8s: pet_idle yields chat→pet (if chat was visible).
- t=10s, 20s, ...: rotate switches pet↔particle.
- t=60s: standby triggers (fades to clock).

This all coexists fine. The rotate keeps switching pet↔particle every 10s until 60s, then standby fades over. Good.

One concern: when standby is visible, the rotate_timer_cb has `if (standby_view_is_visible()) return;` (my Edit D). And pet_idle_timer_cb — does it need a similar guard? pet_idle_timer_cb checks `if (!s_state.initialized || !s_state.screen_visible) return;` (line 305). When standby is visible, screen_visible is false (chat not visible), so pet_idle_timer_cb returns early. Good, no conflict.

But wait — when standby is visible, what's `s_state.screen_visible`? It's still false (chat was yielded). And `s_state.approval_visible` false. So rotate checks screen_visible (false, passes), approval_visible (false, passes), s_last_pet_state (0, passes), then `standby_view_is_visible()` (true, returns). Good. So rotate is suspended during standby. 

Now, what about the pet/particle's own timers (pet_idle_timer, physics timer, breathe anim)? During standby, the pet/particle screens are NOT active (standby screen is active), but their lv_timers still run (pet_idle_timer_cb checks screen_visible; physics timer_cb checks `s_pf.initialized && s_pf.visible`). When standby shows, `pet_status_view`'s `visible` is still true (we didn't hide it), and `particle_flow_view`'s visible is true if it was showing. So their timers keep running in the background (breathe anim, physics step) — but they're on non-active screens, so LVGL doesn't flush them (only the active screen is rendered). So no visual conflict, just some wasted CPU. That's acceptable (same as how pet keeps animating behind chat? No — actually pet's show_async sets visible=true and start_anim_for; when chat shows, pet is hidden via pet_status_view_hide? Let me not over-analyze; the existing design already has pet/particle animating while chat is up in some flows).

Actually, wait — let me reconsider. When standby shows via `standby_view_show()`, it does `lv_screen_load_anim(s_sb.screen, FADE_IN, ...)`. This changes the active screen from pet/particle to standby. The pet/particle screens remain "loaded" (not deleted) but inactive. Their `visible` flags remain true. Their timers (breathe/float/physics) keep running but render nothing (inactive screen). This wastes some CPU but is harmless. Actually the pet's `start_anim_for` breathe/float use `lv_anim` which calls `lv_obj_set_style_opa`/`translate` on the sprite — these trigger invalidate on the INACTIVE screen. LVGL will mark it dirty but not flush (since not active). Actually, invalidating an object on an inactive screen: LVGL's `lv_obj_invalidate` calls `lv_obj_invalidate` which walks up to find the screen and invalidates on the display. Hmm, this could cause a full invalidate of the display even for inactive screens, leading to re-render of the ACTIVE screen? No — the invalidation is area-based on the display, and the renderer renders the active screen's content in that area. Since the pet sprite is at a different location than the standby clock, invalidating the pet sprite's area on the display would cause a re-render of... the active screen (standby) in that area. The standby screen has nothing there (or its bg), so it re-renders the standby bg. This is essentially a no-op visually but does trigger a flush of that partial area.

This is getting into deep territory. The key question: does having pet/particle animating "behind" the standby screen cause the white-sweep or any visual artifact? In PARTIAL render mode (which we're switching to), only dirty areas are flushed. The pet breathe anim changes opacity → invalidates sprite area → partial flush of that area. But the active screen is standby, so the flush would write the standby screen's content at that area (which is just the dark bg, since standby's widgets are elsewhere). So it'd be a dark flush, no white. Acceptable, but slightly wasteful.

To be safe and clean, should I STOP the pet/particle animations when entering standby? That would be the "elegant" thing (standby = everything sleeps). But it adds complexity: I'd need to call `pet_status_view_hide()` and `particle_flow_view_hide()` when entering standby. But hide() does `lv_screen_load_anim(prev_screen, ...)` which would switch active screen BACK to prev (fighting the standby screen load).

Hmm. Actually, the cleanest is: when standby shows, also hide pet/particle (set their `visible=false` without reloading prev). But the existing hide() API always reloads prev_screen, which would conflict.

Let me step back. The simplest robust approach that avoids the "inactive screen animating" issue: DON'T worry about it. The pet breathe/float and particle physics are subtle opacity/position changes on inactive screens. In PARTIAL mode, they'll cause occasional small dark flushes. Not visible as white sweep. The prior "white sweep" was FULL render mode re-flushing the ENTIRE screen every animation frame. PARTIAL mode fixes that fundamentally. The standby screen itself is mostly static (1s clock update = tiny text region flush).

Actually, wait — there's a more important subtlety I need to handle: when standby is visible, the pet's breathe anim (opacity 255→190→255 over 1.8s) and float anim (translate ±2px over 2.6s) run CONTINUOUSLY. These invalidate the pet sprite area every frame. In PARTIAL mode, this means ~every frame, a partial flush of the pet sprite area happens. The pet sprite is ~96×96 px in the center of the screen. The standby clock is ALSO roughly in the center. So the pet sprite area OVERLAPS the clock area. So the pet's continuous anim would keep flushing the center region, re-rendering the STANDBY screen's clock there. That's fine visually (the clock is there), but it means the standby screen is NOT actually "sleeping" — the LCD is still being driven continuously by the pet's background animation.

This matters for the "standby" intent (dim, calm, minimal power). But more practically, it means: does it cause tearing/flicker? No — it just re-flushes the center region with the same clock content. It's wasteful but not broken.

However, I think for correctness and elegance, I SHOULD pause the pet/particle when standby is active. The cleanest way without touching the existing hide() semantics: add explicit "pause" via the existing state mechanism. Actually, the simplest: when standby_timer_cb fires and shows standby, ALSO stop the rotate (already done via is_visible check) and stop the pet/particle by... hmm.

Actually, let me reconsider. Is there a simpler mental model? The pet breathe/float only animate while `s_pet.visible` is true AND pet screen was shown. When we load the standby screen on top, pet stays visible. 

I think the cleanest minimal-risk solution: in `standby_view_show`'s `show_async_cb`, after loading the standby screen, also hide the pet and particle screens WITHOUT restoring prev (i.e., just set their visible=false and stop their anims). But that requires a new "silent hide" API on pet/particle, OR I can call the existing `pet_status_view_hide()`/`particle_flow_view_hide()` — but those reload prev_screen, which after standby is loaded would reload... the pet's prev_screen (whatever it was before pet was shown, possibly the chat or nothing).

This is getting complicated. Let me reconsider the scope and risk.

Given the primary requirement is "去掉白底刷屏" (fix the white sweep) + "长时间无操作进入待机" (standby after idle), and the white sweep is fixed by PARTIAL mode, the standby screen's elegance is secondary. The background pet animation causing redundant center-region flushes is NOT a white sweep (PARTIAL mode + it's the standby content being re-flushed, which is dark). So it won't reintroduce the white sweep.

But there IS one risk: the pet's `float_cb` does `lv_obj_set_style_translate_y(o, amp, 0)` — this invalidates the sprite area. The particle `physics_step` does `lv_obj_set_pos` on particles. These are all on inactive screens. In LVGL, invalidating an object on a non-active screen — does it even reach the display's dirty area? Let me think about LVGL v9 internals: `lv_obj_invalidate` calls `lv_obj_invalidate(obj)` → computes area → `lv_obj_invalidate(area)`. The `lv_obj_invalidate` function invalidates on the obj's screen's display. For an object on a non-active screen, the invalidation still marks the display dirty in that area. Then `lv_refr` (the refresh) renders the ACTIVE screen. So yes, it causes a re-render+flush of that area of the active screen.

Actually, hmm, I'm not 100% sure LVGL invalidates for inactive screens. There might be a check. But regardless, even in the worst case, it's a dark re-flush, not white.

Let me make a pragmatic decision: I will ALSO stop the pet/particle activity when standby shows, by adding simple "pause" behavior. But rather than a new API, I'll do it in the standby show path via the EXISTING hide functions but guarded so they don't fight.

Actually, the truly clean and minimal approach: In `standby_timer_cb`, before `standby_view_show()`, call the existing hide functions is wrong (prev_screen conflict). 

Let me look at what `pet_status_view_hide` does more carefully:
```c
static void hide_async_cb(void *data) {
  if (!s_pet.initialized || !s_pet.visible) return;
  stop_anim();
  if (s_pet.prev_screen)
    lv_screen_load_anim(s_pet.prev_screen, ...);
  s_pet.visible = false;
}
```

If I call `pet_status_view_hide()` while standby is being shown, the sequence via async:
1. `standby_view_show()` → queues `show_async_cb` (loads standby, sets s_sb.visible=true).

/**
 * standby_view.h — 待机界面（暗色数字时钟）。
 *
 * 长时间无操作后(由 lvgl_ui_channel.c 的 60s 空闲计时器触发),主界面渐隐渐显
 * 切到一块极简的暗色数字时钟(大号 HH:MM + 日期 + "待机中"提示),比宠物/粒子页
 * 更暗更静,一眼可辨是"睡了"。任意真实交互都会调 standby_view_hide() 渐隐渐显

 *

 * cold-start 或 set_page 逻辑加载;退出时记住并恢复 show 前的活动屏。
 */

#pragma once

#include <stdbool.h>

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

/**
 * 初始化待机屏(暗色数字时钟),但不加载。首次 show 前必须 init,重复调用幂等。
 * 必须在 LVGL 线程(LVGL 已初始化后)调用。
 */
int standby_view_init(void);

/**
 * 渐隐渐显进入待机屏(记住当前活动屏)。重复调用(已可见)为 no-op。
 * 线程安全:异步调度到 LVGL 线程。
 */
void standby_view_show(void);

/**
 * 渐隐渐显退出待机屏,恢复 show 前的活动屏。重复调用(已隐藏)为 no-op。
 * 线程安全:异步调度到 LVGL 线程。
 */
void standby_view_hide(void);

/**
 * 待机屏当前是否可见。
 */
bool standby_view_is_visible(void);

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

/**
 * standby_view.h — 待机界面（暗色数字时钟）。
 *
 * 长时间无操作后(由 lvgl_ui_channel.c 的 60s 空闲计时器触发),主界面渐隐渐显
 * 切到一块极简的暗色数字时钟(大号 HH:MM + 日期 + "待机中"提示),比宠物/粒子页
 * 更暗更静,一眼可辨是"睡了"。任意真实交互都会调 standby_view_hide() 渐隐渐显
 * 回先前页面。
 *
 * 与主腿的关系:本模块是一个独立 LVGL 屏幕,只在空闲超时后被 show,不被任何
 * cold-start 或 set_page 逻辑加载;退出时记住并恢复 show 前的活动屏。
 */

#pragma once

#include <stdbool.h>

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

/**
 * 初始化待机屏(暗色数字时钟),但不加载。首次 show 前必须 init,重复调用幂等。
 * 必须在 LVGL 线程(LVGL 已初始化后)调用。
 */
int standby_view_init(void);

/**
 * 渐隐渐显进入待机屏(记住当前活动屏)。重复调用(已可见)为 no-op。
 * 线程安全:异步调度到 LVGL 线程。
 */
void standby_view_show(void);

/**
 * 渐隐渐显退出待机屏,恢复 show 前的活动屏。重复调用(已隐藏)为 no-op。
 * 线程安全:异步调度到 LVGL 线程。
 */
void standby_view_hide(void);

/**
 * 待机屏当前是否可见。
 */
bool standby_view_is_visible(void);

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

# BK7258 Worktree Build

## Complete workflow

Prefer the bundled end-to-end wrapper. Without `--flash` it performs the safe
build, L1 validation, package, independent decode, and package-integrity gate:

```bash
<skill-dir>/scripts/full_flow.sh \
  --workspace <openvela-workspace> \
  --worktree <feature-worktree> \
  --jobs 12
```

The wrapper derives one stable slot per worktree under
`cmake_out/bk7258-worktrees/`. Its `build/cp` and optional `build/ap` directories
are reused for normal Vela incremental builds, and its `package` directory is
safely replaced on each successful package run. A binding file ties the slot to
the canonical workspace/worktree paths, so another worktree cannot reuse it.
If a component defconfig changes, only that component's generated build cache
is recreated. Use `--fresh` to deliberately recreate this worktree's generated
build cache. Use `--slot NAME` only to choose a stable human-readable slot.

To flash, rerun in an interactive terminal and explicitly add `--flash`:

```bash
<skill-dir>/scripts/full_flow.sh \
  --workspace <openvela-workspace> \
  --worktree <feature-worktree> \
  --flash --device /dev/ttyUSB0
```

To flash an existing verified package without rebuilding or requiring a
workspace/worktree, give the image and the board tools directory explicitly:

```bash
<skill-dir>/scripts/full_flow.sh \
  --image /absolute/path/to/all-app.bin \
  --tools-dir /absolute/path/to/board/bk7258-devkit/tools \
  --flash --device /dev/ttyUSB0
```

Image-only mode requires `manifest.json` and `decode-report.json` next to the
image. It runs the same independent integrity gate and automatic flash wrapper
but skips build/package. `--worktree <feature-worktree>` may replace
`--tools-dir`; the wrapper then derives `board/bk7258-devkit/tools` from that
worktree.

Flashing is destructive and must use an interactive terminal. The PTY wrapper
streams the loader output without buffering and drives the reset itself: once
the loader prints `connect success`, the wrapper opens the same serial device
as a second writer and injects `reboot bootloader` into the running NSH
console. Target firmware carrying the bootloader-reset patch
(`feature/bk7258-bootloader-reset`, `board_reset`
`ENTER_BOOTLOADER` via AON WDT) then performs a chip-level reset with the
vendor warm-jump tag cleared and the reset reason recorded as watchdog, so
the BootROM runs the cold chain and BL2 opens the download listen window
that the already-polling loader catches by itself -- no manual reset.
`Gotten Bus...` produces the handshake-success banner. If the automatic
reset does not engage within a few seconds (firmware without the patch, a
hung console), the wrapper retries once and then falls back to bell-and-
prompt manual resets, numbered 1, 2, ...; press reset on each prompt and
stop after the success banner. Never press reset after `Begin EraseFlash`,
and never type into the terminal during the automatic phase.

The public workflow assumes a trusted, current-user-owned workspace and Git
worktree. It does not defend against malicious processes running as the same
Unix user, SIGKILL, power loss, or tools that ignore its mapping lock. It never
runs worktree scripts through `sudo` and refuses to
run as root. Give the normal user access to the serial device through the
platform's serial-device group (commonly `dialout`). Before writing, the
wrapper verifies the audited `bk_loader` SHA-256, prints the complete image
SHA-256. The explicit `--flash` flag is the authorization switch. The agent
must still announce the target device and complete image hash in commentary
immediately before launching it.

When an agent launches the flash stage for the user, it must first announce in
commentary the target device, the complete image SHA-256, and that the wrapper
injects `reboot bootloader` automatically (manual-reset fallback prompts
appear only if the auto reset does not engage), then run the command with
interactive terminal support. Never launch `--flash` in the background,
through redirected output, or in a non-interactive shell. Keep the turn open
until `Writing Flash OK` or a clear failure is reported.

The existing board scripts remain the authority: `bk7258-package.sh` must
produce `decode pass`, and `bk7258-flash.sh` must reproduce the report, validate
all hashes, save the loader log, and find `Writing Flash OK`.

## Scope

This workflow is for a BK7258 team-repository worktree whose sources are
linked into the parent OpenVela workspace. The parent workspace is the
directory containing both `build.sh` and `nuttx/`; it is not the team-repository
checkout and not the worktree directory itself.

Never build a BK7258 worktree by passing `board/bk7258-devkit/configs/cp` to
`build.sh`. That path is valid for repository-local Python tools, but
`build.sh`/`lunch` resolves board configs through the manifest path under
`vendor/beken/boards/...`.

## 1. Establish the worktree mapping

For normal worktree builds, use the bundled wrapper; it serializes access to
the shared mapping and restores both links on exit:

```bash
<skill-dir>/scripts/build_worktree.sh \
  --workspace <openvela-workspace> \
  --worktree <feature-worktree> \
  --component cp \
  --jobs 12
```

Use `--component ap` for AP. Use `--output /absolute/output/path` only for an
isolated build whose artifacts will be passed explicitly to packaging.

From the parent OpenVela workspace, verify the mapped paths:

```bash
readlink -f vendor/beken/chips/bk7258
readlink -f vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit
```

For a feature worktree, both targets must resolve into that worktree:

```text
<worktree>/chips/bk7258
<worktree>/board/bk7258-devkit
```

If they point at another checkout, stop and resolve the mapping before
building. In a shared workspace, changing symlinks is visible to other
processes. Prefer a serialized build, save both original link targets, and
restore them in a shell `trap` even when the build fails. Do not delete the
symlink targets or use a broad recursive cleanup.

The project manifest is the source of truth for the normal mapping. The build
tree consumes the mapped `vendor/` paths, while packaging scripts may be run
from the worktree because they locate the workspace by the `build.sh` and
`nuttx/` markers.

## 2. Configure and build CP/AP

Run from the parent workspace. Use the mapped path and keep the trailing slash:

```bash
./build.sh vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit/configs/cp/ --cmake -j12
./build.sh vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit/configs/ap/ --cmake -j12
```

For a CP-only or Wi-Fi-disabled platform change, the first command is the
minimum build. Confirm the generated `.config` does not enable Wi-Fi/WPA when
the acceptance requires a normal CP configuration with Wi-Fi disabled.

`build.sh` derives output names from the board/config selection. Do not add a
random `-b` directory unless the task explicitly needs isolation:

```text
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/bk7258/app.bin
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/bk7258/nuttx.elf
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/bk7258/l1-validation.json
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_ap/bk7258_ap/app1.bin
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_ap/bk7258_ap/l1-validation.json
```

The normal build command supplies the project environment and compiler wrapper.
Direct `cmake --build` can fail with missing `ccache` or stale source paths and
is not equivalent evidence.

## 3. Package and independently decode

The default flow builds and packages the real CP plus OpenVela AP AMP image.
The bundled AP placeholder is recovery-only and must be selected explicitly
with `--placeholder`; it is expected to fail CPU1 AP release validation at
runtime.

For the repository-bundled recovery package, the project wrapper is the
preferred path:

```bash
<worktree>/board/bk7258-devkit/tools/bk7258-package.sh
```

It reads the CP/AP outputs, selects the real OpenVela AP profile, and runs the
independent decoder. The wrapper must print `decode       pass` before an image
is considered valid.

The default package slot intentionally replaces its previous package after the
new CP/AP build and L1 validation pass. `all-app.bin`, `manifest.json`, and
`decode-report.json` remain bound and are verified together before flashing.
Copy that trio elsewhere explicitly when a run must be preserved as historical
hardware evidence.

The package wrapper validates both L1 reports, invokes the container packer,
and independently decodes the final linear-CRC image. Do not flash `app.bin`
or `app1.bin` directly.

## 4. Offline regression checks

Run from the parent workspace or pass paths explicitly:

```bash
python3 <worktree>/board/bk7258-devkit/tests/test_bk7258_bundled_packaging.py
```

The decoder must produce the same report for relative and absolute input paths.
The report normalizes `image.path` with `Path.resolve()`; do not regress this
to the caller's spelling of the path, because evidence hashes and reports must
be stable across invocation directories.

For the vendor-input profile, first validate the machine-local input file and
then run the profile/package test described in
`board/bk7258-devkit/packaging/README.md`. Never invent vendor input paths or
copy credentials into the repository.

## 5. Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `No config file found at` | `build.sh` received `board/...` instead of mapped `vendor/...` path, or the path lacks the expected config directory | Run from the parent workspace with `vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit/configs/cp/` or `ap/` and verify `readlink -f` |
| Early `grep: dor/.../defconfig: No such file` followed by a valid `lunch`, build, and L1 pass | `build.sh` has a non-fatal path-slicing check before `lunch` for full mapped paths | Judge the final command result; do not treat this line alone as failure. A later `No config file found at` or nonzero build result is still a real failure |
| Output builds the wrong source checkout | Shared `vendor/` symlink points at another worktree | Save/replace the two BK7258 links for the build, serialize the operation, and restore them with a trap |
| Image size/config unexpectedly changes while build still passes | A standard CMake output directory retained another worktree's `.config` | Use `full_flow.sh`; its binding prevents cross-worktree cache reuse, and defconfig changes rebuild only the affected component slot |
| `ccache: not found` from direct CMake | Bypassed the environment setup used by `build.sh` | Re-run through `./build.sh ... --cmake` |
| CP image not found during packaging | CP build was not successful or used a custom output directory | Check `cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/bk7258/app.bin`, its L1 report, and pass `--cp-app-bin` when using `-b` |
| Decoder report differs by working directory | Decoder received relative input and stored it verbatim | Use the current decoder that resolves `args.image`; run the path-stability regression |
| Too many generated directories | A one-shot workflow was used instead of the stable bound slot | Use the default `full_flow.sh`; it incrementally reuses one build slot and replaces one package slot per worktree |
| `Getting Bus...` keeps printing but `Gotten Bus...` never appears, then the manual-reset banner shows up | The automatic `reboot bootloader` did not engage: target firmware lacks the bootloader-reset patch, its console was hung, or the injection window was missed | Press reset on each numbered bell/banner from `notify_flash.py`; stop resetting after `Gotten Bus...`. Deploy `feature/bk7258-bootloader-reset` firmware for the automatic path |
| No reset prompt and no auto-reset banner are visible | Flash was launched without a PTY or through a buffered pipe | Run `full_flow.sh --flash` in an interactive terminal; do not redirect loader stdout |
| `GetBus fail` or `LinkCheck Timeout` | Reset timing, USB, downloader mode, or a busy serial port prevented handshake; Flash has not been erased yet | Close serial monitors and rerun the interactive flash stage |
| Flash refuses root or reports serial permission denied | Public workflow does not execute mutable worktree code as root | Add the user to the serial-device group, re-login, and run without `sudo` |
| Loader SHA-256 mismatch | The bundled proprietary loader differs from the audited repository version | Stop; review the binary change and update the pinned hash only through code review |

## Acceptance boundary

A successful host build proves compilation and L1 image validation only. A
passing package/decode proves the linear-CRC container contract. Hardware IRQ,
register readback, GPIO waveform, cold boot, and UART behavior require separate

## Complete workflow

```bash
  --workspace <openvela-workspace> \
  --worktree <feature-worktree> \
  --jobs 12
```

The wrapper derives one stable slot per worktree under
`cmake_out/bk7258-worktrees/`. Its `build/cp` and optional `build/ap` directories
are reused for normal Vela incremental builds, and its `package` directory is
safely replaced on each successful package run. A binding file ties the slot to
the canonical workspace/worktree paths, so another worktree cannot reuse it.
If a component defconfig changes, only that component's generated build cache
is recreated. Use `--fresh` to deliberately recreate this worktree's generated
build cache. Use `--slot NAME` only to choose a stable human-readable slot.

To flash, rerun in an interactive terminal and explicitly add `--flash`:

```bash
<skill-dir>/scripts/full_flow.sh \
  --workspace <openvela-workspace> \
  --worktree <feature-worktree> \
  --flash --device /dev/ttyUSB0
```

To flash an existing verified package without rebuilding or requiring a
workspace/worktree, give the image and the board tools directory explicitly:

```bash
<skill-dir>/scripts/full_flow.sh \
  --image /absolute/path/to/all-app.bin \
  --tools-dir /absolute/path/to/board/bk7258-devkit/tools \
  --flash --device /dev/ttyUSB0
```

Image-only mode requires `manifest.json` and `decode-report.json` next to the
image. It runs the same independent integrity gate and automatic flash wrapper
but skips build/package. `--worktree <feature-worktree>` may replace
`--tools-dir`; the wrapper then derives `board/bk7258-devkit/tools` from that
worktree.

Flashing is destructive and must use an interactive terminal. The PTY wrapper
streams the loader output without buffering and drives the reset itself: once
the loader prints `connect success`, the wrapper opens the same serial device
as a second writer and injects `reboot bootloader` into the running NSH
console. Target firmware carrying the bootloader-reset patch
(`feature/bk7258-bootloader-reset`, `board_reset`
`ENTER_BOOTLOADER` via AON WDT) then performs a chip-level reset with the
vendor warm-jump tag cleared and the reset reason recorded as watchdog, so
the BootROM runs the cold chain and BL2 opens the download listen window
that the already-polling loader catches by itself -- no manual reset.
`Gotten Bus...` produces the handshake-success banner. If the automatic
reset does not engage within a few seconds (firmware without the patch, a
hung console), the wrapper retries once and then falls back to bell-and-
prompt manual resets, numbered 1, 2, ...; press reset on each prompt and
stop after the success banner. Never press reset after `Begin EraseFlash`,
and never type into the terminal during the automatic phase.

The public workflow assumes a trusted, current-user-owned workspace and Git
worktree. It does not defend against malicious processes running as the same
Unix user, SIGKILL, power loss, or tools that ignore its mapping lock. It never
runs worktree scripts through `sudo` and refuses to
run as root. Give the normal user access to the serial device through the
platform's serial-device group (commonly `dialout`). Before writing, the
wrapper verifies the audited `bk_loader` SHA-256, prints the complete image

## Scope

This workflow is for a BK7258 team-repository worktree whose sources are
linked into the parent OpenVela workspace. The parent workspace is the
directory containing both `build.sh` and `nuttx/`; it is not the team-repository
checkout and not the worktree directory itself.

Never build a BK7258 worktree by passing `board/bk7258-devkit/configs/cp` to

## 1. Establish the worktree mapping

For normal worktree builds, use the bundled wrapper; it serializes access to
